raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #65684. The Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe named its day-0 images only in an install note, so the builder's commands used `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on NVIDIA. This pins the images, hides the pip tab, and adds Vera Rubin (VR200) with its CUDA 13.4 image.

## Claims

| Hardware | Image before | Image after |
|---|---|---|
| GB300, B300 | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` | `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31` |
| VR200 (new, `supported`) | not offered | `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134` |
| MI355X | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` | unchanged, now from `model.docker_image.amd` |
| 810E, M890 | PPU image | unchanged |

- The pip tab is gone on all hardware, because K3.1 isn't in a wheel until #65685 lands.
- The builder no longer offers a CUDA 12.9 toggle for a `kimi-k31-cu129` tag that doesn't exist.

## Validation

Recipe metadata only; no serving-engine code changes, so there are no model evaluation results. **Nothing was run on VR200**, which is why it is `supported` rather than `verified`. CI has no Rubin hardware either.

Run from vllm-project/recipes at `main` (f382387), which has the `vr200` profile:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes
# ✓ vllm recipes from <vllm>/recipes are valid against the renderer
```

- **Before/after diff:** I built the JSON API from `origin/main` and from this branch, then compared every Kimi-K3.1-Pro rendering. On existing hardware the only rendering differences are the image tags above. VR200 adds its own new files.
- **VR200 rendering:** it opens on `multi_node_tp` (TP8 over 2 trays). PD uses 2 prefill and 4 decode trays, the same as GB300.
- **Markdown form:** the `.md` rendering shows no `uv pip` command on GB300, VR200 or MI355X.
- **Docker Hub:** `vllm-openai:kimi-k31` and `kimi-k31-cu134` both publish amd64 and arm64; `vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` publishes amd64.

## Details

- **`min_vllm_version: "0.34.0"`:** this replaces `"nightly"`, which `cu129DockerImage` scores as 0.0.0, so it would derive a `-cu129` tag. 0.34.0 assumes K3.1 ships in the first release after v0.33.0, and `nightly_required` stays set until then.
- **`install: { pip: false }` on `vr200`:** pip is already off for the whole recipe. This override is there to replace the profile's note, which says its own `cu134-nightly` image is the only one that runs on Rubin.
- **Rubin flags:** `rubin` shares the `blackwell` block (`--load-format fastsafetensors` and the 3600 s ready timeout), following #65400. Without it, loading ~1.56 TB could hit the default timeout. It has not been tuned on Rubin, and there is no DCP row on VR200 because DCP sizes list only the GPUs it ran on.
- **Conflict with #65685:** that PR still adds its own older copy of this file. Its rebase should keep the version on `main`, or it will undo this fix.
- **Not a duplicate:** the open-PR searches for `Kimi-K3.1-Pro` and `kimi-k31` find only #65685, which doesn't contain these changes.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR. The submitter reviews it through this PR.

files.patch:
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@ meta:
   provider: "Moonshot AI"
   description: "2.8T-parameter native multimodal MoE with Kimi Delta Attention, sparse MLA, and a 1M-token context window"
   date_added: 2026-11-02
-  date_updated: 2026-11-04
+  date_updated: 2026-11-05
   tasks:
     - multimodal
     - text
@@ -15,18 +15,25 @@ meta:
   default_hardware: gb300
   hardware:
     gb300: verified
+    vr200: supported
     810e: verified
     m890: verified
 
 model:
   model_id: "moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro"
-  min_vllm_version: "nightly"
+  # The first release after v0.33.0, which K3.1 missed. A number, not "nightly":
+  # the renderer reads "nightly" as 0.0.0 and would offer a `kimi-k31-cu129` tag
+  # that doesn't exist.
+  min_vllm_version: "0.34.0"
   nightly_required: true
+  # Day-0 images published with the release. NVIDIA's is a CUDA 13 (cu130) build
+  # only; AMD's is ROCm 10.0.
+  docker_image:
+    nvidia: "vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31"
+    amd: "vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31"
+  # Docker-only: K3.1 support isn't in a wheel yet (vllm-project/vllm#65685).
   install:
-    docker:
-      note: "Use `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31` (multi-arch; CUDA 13 / cu130 build only). For CUDA 13.4 (Rubin) use `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134`. On MI355X use `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31`."
-    pip:
-      note: "Use a K3.1-enabled vLLM nightly after the integration lands."
+    pip: false
   architecture: moe
   parameter_count: "2.8T"
   active_parameters: "16 experts/token + shared (of 896 routed)"
@@ -97,7 +104,7 @@ variants:
     precision: mxfp4
     # 1561 GB of safetensors x 1.2.
     vram_minimum_gb: 1874
-    supported_hardware: [b300, gb300, mi355x, 810e, m890]
+    supported_hardware: [b300, gb300, vr200, mi355x, 810e, m890]
     description: "MXFP4 routed-expert weights (~1.56 TB on disk); attention, shared experts and the vision tower stay in BF16."
     hardware_overrides:
       810e:
@@ -108,9 +115,12 @@ variants:
         docker_image: "egslingjun-registry.cn-wulanchabu.cr.aliyuncs.com/egslingjun-tmp/inference-xpu-pytorch:kimi-k3.1-pro-vllm0.32.0-cuda13.0-pytorch2.13.0-20261103"
         docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
         install: { pip: false }
-      # Day-0 ROCm 10.0 image published with the release.
-      mi355x:
-        docker_image: "vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31"
+      # The CUDA 13.4 build of this model's image; the Rubin stack needs CUDA 13.4.
+      # This `install` also replaces the profile's note, which names its own
+      # nightly image as the only one that runs on Rubin.
+      vr200:
+        docker_image: "vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134"
+        install: { pip: false }
 
 compatible_strategies:
   - single_node_tp
@@ -135,7 +145,7 @@ strategy_hardware:
     810e: unsupported
     m890: unsupported
 
-# One B300 or MI355X node (8 GPUs) or two GB300 trays (2 x 4 GPUs) hold the checkpoint.
+# One B300 or MI355X node (8 GPUs) or two GB300 / VR200 trays (2 x 4 GPUs) hold the checkpoint.
 strategy_min_gpus:
   single_node_tp: 8
   single_node_tep: 8
@@ -146,13 +156,15 @@ strategy_min_gpus:
 default_strategy: single_node_tp
 
 hardware_overrides:
-  blackwell:
+  blackwell: &k31_blackwell
     extra_args:
       - "--load-format"
       - "fastsafetensors"
     extra_env:
       # Loading ~1.56 TB of weights from network storage can take over 20 minutes.
       VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "3600"
+  # Rubin takes the Blackwell configuration. Not tuned on Rubin yet.
+  rubin: *k31_blackwell
   amd:
     extra_env:
       VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER: "1"
@@ -334,22 +346,24 @@ strategy_overrides:
       - "flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided"
 
   # PD pools: a TP8 prefill pool with expert parallelism (one B300 node or two
-  # GB300 trays) and a DEP16 decode pool — TP1 x DP16 with expert parallelism
-  # (two B300 nodes or four GB300 trays). NIXL moves the KDA short-conv state
-  # in three reads, which needs the DS conv state layout.
+  # GB300 / VR200 trays) and a DEP16 decode pool — TP1 x DP16 with expert
+  # parallelism (two B300 nodes or four GB300 / VR200 trays). NIXL moves the KDA
+  # short-conv state in three reads, which needs the DS conv state layout.
   pd_cluster:
     env:
       VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT: "DS"
     prefill:
       nodes:
         b300: 1    # 1 B300 node = 8 GPUs
         gb300: 2   # 2 GB300 trays = 8 GPUs
+        vr200: 2   # 2 VR200 trays = 8 GPUs
       parallelism: tep
       tp: 8
     decode:
       nodes:
         b300: 2    # 2 B300 nodes = 16 GPUs
         gb300: 4   # 4 GB300 trays = 16 GPUs
+        vr200: 4   # 4 VR200 trays = 16 GPUs
       parallelism: dep
       tp: 1
 
@@ -364,6 +378,9 @@ guide: |
   The baseline is the simplest working setup on NVIDIA: one tensor-parallel group of 8 GPUs,
   either two GB300 trays or one B300 node. Throughput was not tuned.
 
+  VR200 (preview) takes the same TP8 layout on two trays, in the `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-cu134`
+  image (CUDA 13.4). It uses the Blackwell flags and hasn't been tuned or verified on Rubin.
+
   On MI355X, one node takes the same TP8 layout with the AMD profile's AITER environment, in the
   day-0 `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` image. So far only the
   [AgentX TP8](#preset-mi355x_agentx) configuration has run on MI355X: the tuned single-node AgentX
